generated_output.summary: In the Kimi VSCode extension, typing a slash command like `/[skill-name]` followed by the `Tab` key incorrectly submits the chat message instead of triggering autocompletion or selecting the active skill suggestion.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The issue stems from the keydown event handling in the webview's chat input interface (likely handling `Tab` and `Enter` key codes), where default key behaviors are not intercepted to prevent message submission when autocomplete menus or skill popups are open.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect webview keydown event handler
step_by_step_plan.description: Examine symbol KimiWebviewProvider and its webview message or HTML template generation in apps/vscode/src/KimiWebviewProvider.ts to locate where keyboard events ('Tab' and 'Enter') for chat input and slash command autocompletion are bound.

step_by_step_plan.title: Intercept Tab and Enter keys during active skill suggestion
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the keydown listener in the webview script within KimiWebviewProvider.ts to check if a slash command or skill suggestion dropdown is currently open and active, preventing default message submission on Tab or Enter.

step_by_step_plan.title: Verify extension activation and command setup
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect activate in apps/vscode/src/extension.ts to ensure webview provider registration and command message listeners correctly handle selection messages from the webview UI.

step_by_step_plan.title: Execute test suite to verify no regressions
step_by_step_plan.description: Run the repository test suite using the verified test command to validate the webview integration and input handling logic.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Preventing the browser's default behavior for specific keys like Tab or Enter inside input fields.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Essential for building custom autocomplete and suggestion widgets so that pressing Tab doesn't jump focus or submit forms unintentionally.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Fixing the bug requires intercepting `Tab` (and optionally `Enter`) keydown events when the skill suggestion popup is open and calling `event.preventDefault()`.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The communication channel between the VSCode extension host and the embedded React/web frontend.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Enables UI components inside the webview to interact with extension commands and workspace APIs.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Understanding how input events are captured within the webview UI components helps pinpoint where keyboard listeners are attached.

common_pitfalls: Forgetting to check whether a suggestion dropdown is actually active before intercepting Tab or Enter keys.
Breaking standard accessibility navigation by unconditionally swallowing Tab key events.
